question: A 31-year-old man comes to the emergency department for acute tearing chest pain that radiates to the back. Despite appropriate therapy, the patient dies. Autopsy shows an increase in mucoid extracellular matrix and loss of smooth muscle cell nuclei in the media of large arteries. Which of the following additional findings is most likely in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Acute tearing chest pain radiating to the back" -> "Aortic dissection" -> "Loss of smooth muscle cell nuclei in the media of large arteries" -> "Marfan syndrome" -> "Inferonasal lens dislocation" -> 80% CHAIN: "Increase in mucoid extracellular matrix in large arteries" -> "Cystic medial necrosis" -> "Marfan syndrome" -> "Inferonasal lens dislocation" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with acute tearing chest pain that radiates to the back, along with the autopsy findings of an increase in mucoid extracellular matrix and loss of smooth muscle cell nuclei in the media of large arteries, is suggestive of aortic dissection. Aortic dissection can lead to catastrophic outcomes despite appropriate therapy.
